title: Grind a mounted chip package's cross-section flat on a turning abrasive disc, down to the line scribed round the mount
instruction: Grind the mounted section on the turning paper down to the line scribed round the mount. Hold the mount face down on the paper and press it steadily, moving it back and forth between the centre and the edge of the disc and keeping its face flat, until the face reaches the line all the way round. Then lift it off the paper, set it back on its rest as it started, and move your hand clear.
context: Failure-analysis labs inspect a packaged chip's solder joints, bumps and die by cross-section: the package is sawn, set in an epoxy mount, then ground flat by hand on a grinder-polisher before polishing and microscopy. Buehler's guide to manual preparation asks for 'a firm hand pressure', the specimen 'continually moved back and forth between the center and the edge of the wheel', starting on P180 silicon-carbide paper 'until plane'. Here one hand grinds a 32 mm mount holding a strip sawn from a BGA package on P180 paper turning at 150 rpm, down to a line scribed 0.3 mm above its face: the last 0.3 mm of the P180 step, the pass a technician takes slowly to the line, short of the ball row, leaving stock for the finer grits. The paper drags the mount sideways while the hand pushes it down and sweeps it across a disc that moves faster at its edge; any rocking or tilt grinds a facet instead of one plane, and going past the line spoils the section.
setup: Station: two YAM arms with parallel grippers on a table; the right arm does the work, the left stays at its ready pose. Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left), heights above the table top. A benchtop grinder-polisher: a 40 x 30 x 12 cm body centred at x 33, y -16; on it a splash bowl 32 cm across with its rim 2 cm above the paper, and a 203 mm (8 in) aluminium platen centred at x 28, y -16, covered with P180 SiC paper whose top is 14 cm up, turning anticlockwise seen from above at 150 rpm. The mount: an epoxy cylinder 32 mm across and 35 mm tall, 40 g, with a 20 mm strip sawn from a package set in it edge-on, flush with its face; a red line is scribed round its side 0.3 mm above the face. It stands face down on a 5 x 5 cm rest 6 cm high at x 20, y -42. Wet paper on the mount: friction 0.4 (assumed; 0.3 to 0.7 changes only the drag). Nothing is random (object_jitter=0). Real trial. (a) Grinder: a single-platen 8 in metallographic grinder-polisher run at 150 rpm (for identification only: UKAM SMART CUT LG, Toptech P20G-1-E; machines of this class list at about US$1,600 to 1,900, so the low-cost build below is the route for a repeatable trial), or the low-cost build (motor US$38.95 at Pololu): an 8 in (203 mm) 6061 aluminium disc 6 mm thick on a Pololu #4744 gearmotor (12 V, 70:1, 150 rpm no-load, about 2.6 N m stall; the drag here is under 0.5 N m) with a 6 mm shaft hub, run from a 12 V 2 A supply, in a 32 cm plastic bowl with a 10 mm drain hole and a tube to a bucket, on a 40 x 30 x 12 cm plywood box. A fresh 8 in PSA-backed P180 SiC disc each trial (Buehler CarbiMet PSA P180 8 in, 36-08-0180, or Klingspor 8 in PSA P180 SiC); water about 0.5 L/min from a squeeze bottle or a tap tube onto the platen centre. (b) Mount, made the same way each time: a 20 mm strip cut across an Adafruit Perma-Proto half-size board (#1609, plated through-holes at 2.54 mm pitch), standing edge-on in a 1.25 in (32 mm) silicone mount cup; 17.5 g epoxy resin and 5.25 g hardener (Allied EpoxyMount), cured as the maker says; trimmed to 35 mm. Lines are scribed round its side every 0.3 mm with a height gauge and the face is brought to the next line beforehand, so a trial removes only the last 0.3 mm (about 3 min at about 0.1 mm/min, the same rate as in the simulation); one mount serves several trials. Before each trial the face is inked with a permanent marker, so an unground patch shows. (c) The jaws close on the mount's upper part, commanded to 80 N a finger and held by the harness to its 50 N cap (set values, not a measured YAM figure; a 40 N grip let the mount slide up the fingers), against a drag of about 4 N (0.4 x 11 N push); the real trial uses the gripper's bare pads, or powder-free nitrile finger cots if they slip, and a clear PVC splash sleeve on the wrist. (d) The rest: a 5 x 5 x 6 cm PLA block.
scoring: Scored by effect, from the mount's face. Force, speed and path are not scored. Rungs are cumulative. 0.25: some of the face ground on the turning paper (at least 0.05 mm gone somewhere). 0.5: every point ground (the 2 mm grid and a ring 0.5 mm in from the rim), in one plane: fitted plane within 2 degrees of the original face, no point over 0.10 mm off it. 0.75: that, down to the line: 0.23 to 0.37 mm removed at all four quadrant points (12 mm from the axis), the four within 0.10 mm of each other. 1.0: that, with the mount back on its rest as it started (face down, wholly on the rest's 5 x 5 cm top, axis within 5 degrees of vertical), the hand at least 3 cm away, the mount still for 1 s. 0, and it stays 0: more than 0.37 mm removed at any quadrant point or on a ring 2 mm in from the rim; the mount flung off the platen, dropped or knocked over (one let go of on the turning paper is flung off); a finger at the paper's level over the platen; a push on the platen over 25 N; or a push above 2 N for 0.5 s while the mount is off the paper. Real trial: micrometer (0.01 mm) at the four quadrant points before and after; marker ink on the face, any left is unground; straightedge and feeler gauge for one plane; a photo of the mount on its rest; a video from above and the side shows a fling, a drop or a finger on the paper; the push read on a scale under the grinder.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. Removal is a rule (a simulator cannot remove material): Preston's law (Preston 1927, J. Soc. Glass Technol. 11:214), rate = k (p - p0) v at each point of a 2 mm grid; p from the platen's 20 N/mm spring, spread by the mount's tilt; v from the platen's 150 rpm. p0 = 4.5 kPa and k = 1.9e-10 per Pa are set, not measured, so a flat face loses about 0.1 mm/min at 11 N: 0.3 mm in about 190 s. A real hand is assumed to take the same (0.05 to 0.2 mm/min; order from Buehler's PCB method).
reset_notes: Nothing is random (object_jitter=0). Real trial: fit a fresh P180 disc, ink the mount's face, measure it at the four quadrant points, stand it face down on the rest. A mount left faceted or ground past its next line is refaced flat to the line after it on the same machine by hand, or retired; a trial takes about 3 min of grinding (5 min allowed); a mount gives about 10 trials.
